paper_title: Efficiently Learning One-Hidden-Layer ReLU Networks via SchurPolynomials
statement: 5. Conclusions In this paper, we gave a simple algorithm that learns one-hidden-layer ReLU networks of size k under the Gaussian distribution on Rd to L2 -error  with complexity (dk/)O(k) . While the complexity of our algorithm cannot be qualitatively improved within the class of CSQ algorithms (a natural yet restricted family of algorithms), to the best of our knowledge there is no (known) inherent obstacle ruling out a poly(d, k, 1/) time algorithm. It should be noted that the complexity of the non-CSQ algorithm of Chen et al. (2021) is polynomial in d but exponential in 1/ (even for constant k). The existence of a fully-polynomial time algorithm remains open even for the special case of positive weights, where the best known algorithm (Diakonikolas and Kane, 2020) has 2 runtime poly(d/) + (k/)O(log (k)) .
